design_rationale:
WORKLOG — auto_loan_payment_servicing / task 1 (root problem: auto_ext_payoff_settlement)

STEP 0. DRAW AND SCOPE.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/regional_retail_bank/tasks/auto_loan_payment_servicing --tasks 2 printed for
this task: {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}. The tree is
therefore the root plus one prerequisite problem, and the two drawn factor counts are assigned
auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund 5 and auto_ext_payoff_settlement 4.
Already occupied by task 0: auto_ext_fee_overcharge_correction, auto_ext_call_payment_amount,
auto_ext_autopay_rate_restatement and auto_ext_due_day_realignment, with the fee correction, installment
payment, drafting instruction and due day tools. This task claims what remains and nothing else: the
waiver-coverage refund and the settlement figure, on post_gap_refund_16f4decd and
post_loan_payoff_a84c6454. The two scopes are disjoint in policies and in tools, and together the two
tasks cover all six extended policies of the difficulty.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one number — what it takes to be rid of the loan today.
Nothing he says points at the waiver coverage financed with the loan at funding. The settlement rule
says outright that the figure is fixed only after the refund owed on that coverage stands entered on
the loan's records; the loan record shows the coverage still in force and no refund entry, so the agent
must find the refund policy, work the refund out from the charge financed at funding, the months
remaining, the refundable share and the cancellation fee, enter it against the loan, and only then work
the settlement out on the principal the records then show. An agent that settles first and asks about
the coverage afterwards collects 20702.37 instead of 20308.37 and leaves a different terminal state.
The arithmetic on both sides is reconciled from the ledger and from the borrower's other holdings, not
read off a field.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- auto_cancel_gap and auto_gap_refund are governed by auto_evt_gap_refund alone. Its full_refund_window
  time gate is retired, clause by clause, by this policy's declared overwrite of the sentence "A GAP
  cancellation within gap_cancellation_full_refund_days calendar days after the loan funded refunds the
  whole gap_premium.", which the extended rule replaces with a method that covers the whole domain. The
  one_refund dedup gate stays in force: no auto_gap_refund entry exists on this loan, evidenced by the
  ledger, and the write carries the loan reference as the dedup key.
- auto_payment (the settlement write) is governed by auto_evt_payment_allocation, whose loan_open gate
  requires status active or delinquent — the loan is delinquent, 63 days past due, well short of the
  120 at which the principal would be charged off — and by auto_evt_payoff_and_lien, which fixes no
  gate reaching the payment itself (its release_deadline gate applies to the lien release) and enters as
  policy_scope. The payoff figure it defines, principal plus accrued interest plus fees due, is the
  shape the extended policy refines; the allocation order, fees then interest then principal, is
  inherited and is what the three portions passed to the tool follow. No time gate applies to either
  write, so temporal_feasibility is empty.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object of the refund is the waiver coverage financed with this one loan,
correlated by the loan reference; the loan carries gap_coverage true and gap_premium 795.00, and no
auto_gap_refund entry stands on its ledger, so nothing is being refunded twice. The object of the
settlement is the same loan; the charges it clears are the two late charges of 22.00 standing unpaid
(posted 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-31 for the installments due 2026-07-15 and 2026-08-15), and every
earlier charge on the ledger has already been settled by the payment that followed it. The borrower
holds one auto loan, one checking account and one card, so no sibling object competes.

OWNER CARD. The blueprint fixes who acts: "Waivers, due date changes, payoff posting and lien releases are
agent service actions, while a payment extension is the borrower's signed modification of terms and autopay
enrollment and GAP cancellation are the borrower's own instructions, all completed by the borrower." This
task's two tools follow it exactly: post_gap_refund_16f4decd is owner=user, because cancelling the coverage
financed with his own loan is the borrower's own instruction, and post_loan_payoff_a84c6454 is owner=agent,
because posting a payoff is a service action. The base sentence "cancelling is the borrower's own decision
recorded through an auto_requests row of request_type gap_cancellation that the borrower confirms" is
therefore inherited whole and satisfied rather than overridden: the borrower's own call writes that
auto_requests row, request_type gap_cancellation, request_status confirmed, alongside the refund entry and
the close-out of the coverage. The tree still carries a customer's own write - it is now the prerequisite
problem rather than the root.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root auto_ext_payoff_settlement <- auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund
      kind value_input, gate principal_outstanding, form state
      prerequisite sentence: "The amount required to settle the loan in full is fixed only after the
      refund owed on the waiver coverage financed with the loan stands entered on its records."
      condition: the loan's records carry a refund entry for that coverage and the coverage is no
      longer shown in force. resolved_by post_gap_refund_16f4decd, owner user.
One prerequisite problem, matching the draw; the single edge is value_input, meeting the floor of
max(1-1, 1) = 1. Four-point test on the sentence: it joins this policy's own result to what it waits on
with the ordering connective "only after"; the waiting side is a record-visible state, a refund entry
standing on the loan for the coverage financed with it; it names no tool, no policy id and no code
token; and it is a hard requirement over exactly the coverage financed with this loan, no wider and no
narrower than the condition. Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that state about: only
post_gap_refund_16f4decd enters a refund against a loan, and its own policy says so in its own words
("it is entered against the loan rather than paid out to the borrower, so the loan's unpaid principal
falls by it"). Derivation: the reader sees the settlement rule wait on a refund entry, sees the loan
carrying coverage in force with no such entry on the ledger, and finds the one policy whose write books
it. Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.auto_loans.<loan>.gap_coverage = True
and no auto_gap_refund row anywhere in initial_state.auto_transactions. Topological order: refund, then
settlement. There are no parallel edges to reorder. Deletion sensitivity from the Step 5 run: skipping
the refund leaves the principal at 20443.37 and the settlement at 20702.37 instead of 20308.37.

STEP 3. THE WORLD AND WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW IS THERE.
- customers: one profile, Dorian Whitesell, NC resident, so the state's 15 grace days put the late
  charge on the installment due 2026-07-15 at 2026-07-31 and the one on 2026-08-15 at 2026-08-31.
- auto_loans: one New Vehicle Loan funded 2024-02-09 over 60 months at 6.24 (the 6.49 base for the term
  plus nothing for grade A, less the 0.25 relationship reduction the Premier Checking account earned at
  funding, above the 3.99 floor), 35695.00 financed including the 795.00 waiver charge, installment
  694.07, due day 15, next due 2026-07-15 unsatisfied, 63 days past due and therefore delinquent, and
  the coverage still in force. Remove gap_coverage or seed a refund entry and the only edge of the tree
  vanishes; make the loan current and the settlement clock anchor changes tier.
- auto_transactions, 31 rows: the funding disbursement, 28 scheduled installments whose splits are
  worked at 6.24 on the principal then outstanding for the days since the previous credit, and the two
  late charges standing unpaid. The nine installments credited inside the last twelve months are what
  put the refundable share on its middle rung and the settlement rate on its middle rung; the two
  charges are what the settlement clears; the latest entry, the charge of 2026-08-31, is the date the
  first anchor tier would have used had the checking tier been met.
- checking_accounts / checking_transactions: Premier Checking opened 2021-05-20 with a posted balance of
  3167.25 against the 10000.00 fee-waiver daily balance that tier publishes — deliberately far under,
  so the first limb of both multi-source tiers fails and the three payroll deposits of 3184.90 carry
  the second; the three rent debits of 2129.15 are what the balance equals. The account's age, 63 whole
  months, is what puts the unearned-share convention on the quarter rung rather than the day-count rung.
- card_accounts / card_transactions: Travel Rewards Visa Signature with 9800 unredeemed points (over the
  mid threshold of 5000, under the deep threshold of 25000) and 11 purchases totalling 6950.00 over
  twelve months of which 7 fall in the last three (over the mid count of 3, under the deep count of 12),
  so both card-driven tiers land on their middle rung. The purchase of 2025-11-08 is the near-miss: it
  sits 10 whole months back and counts toward the twelve-month total, while the card payment of
  2026-08-24 is not a purchase, and a careless reader who counted it would make the three-month count 8
  and still not reach the deep count of 12.
- No stamp names any tier's outcome, and no cache trap is used in this task.

FACTOR CARD (tier taken, evidence, and the figure the factor's baseline would have given, from the
Step 5 sensitivity run).
auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund, result 390.00, whole baseline 295.82:
  remaining_months_measure (method, checking): middle tier, the balance of 3167.25 is under the 10000.00
  waiver balance but three recurring deposits posted in the last three months, so exactly one limb
  holds and the months remaining run from the installment then due, 2026-07-15, to the maturity of
  2029-02-15, 31; the baseline takes the term less the 31 whole months since funding, 29, giving 353.00.
  refundable_share_step (parameter): 9 scheduled installments credited in the last twelve months, at
  least the mid count of 8 and fewer than the deep count of 12, so the share is 95 percent; the baseline
  share of 90 percent gives 369.00.
  unearned_share_convention (method, checking): the checking account is 63 whole months old, at least
  the mid seasoning of 48 and under the long seasoning of 120, so the months remaining are taken up to
  the whole quarter above, 33; the baseline measures the unearned part on the whole months remaining,
  giving 365.00.
  cancellation_fee_step (parameter, card): 9800 points and 7 purchases in three months are both over the
  mid thresholds and under the deep, so the fee is 25.00; the baseline fee is the 50.00 the product
  publishes, giving 365.00.
  refund_rounding (method): the loan is 31 whole months old, at least the mid seasoning of 24 and under
  the long seasoning of 36, so the refund is rounded half-up to the whole dollar, 390.00; the baseline
  rounds half-up to the cent, giving 390.39.
  Arithmetic: 795.00 at 95 percent is 755.25; 755.25 times 33 over 60 is 415.3875; less the 25.00 fee is
  390.3875; rounded half-up to the whole dollar, 390.00.
auto_ext_payoff_settlement, result 20308.37, whole baseline 20429.92:
  settlement_clock_anchor (method, checking): middle tier again, so the clock runs from the installment
  then due, 2026-07-15, to today, 63 days; the baseline runs from the last payment credited, 2026-06-14,
  94 days, giving 20410.37.
  settlement_rate_step (parameter, card): card purchases of 6950.00 are at least the mid threshold of
  3000.00 and under the deep threshold of 12000.00, and 9 installments were credited in the last twelve
  months, so the rate is the recorded 6.24 less the published 0.25 automatic-payment reduction, 5.99;
  the baseline is the recorded 6.24, giving 20316.37.
  settlement_transit_allowance (parameter, card): 9800 points and 7 purchases put the allowance on its
  middle rung, 1 day, so the clock runs 64 days; the baseline allowance of 3 days gives 20314.37.
  settlement_interest_rounding (method): the loan is 31 whole months old, so the interest of 210.62 is
  rounded half-up to the whole dollar, 211.00; the baseline rounds to the cent, giving 20307.99.
  Arithmetic: the principal after the refund is entered is 20443.37 - 390.00 = 20053.37; interest is
  20053.37 times 5.99 percent divided by 365 and multiplied by 64, 210.62, rounded to 211.00; with the
  44.00 of charges standing the settlement is 20308.37, split 44.00 to charges, 211.00 to interest and
  20053.37 to principal, which takes the loan to zero on both accounts.
Every declared factor moves its result and every whole-baseline figure differs from gold, so an agent
who finds only a computation document computes a definite wrong number with no signal. Each computation
carries at least two parameter factors, at least two method factors, at least two multi-source factors
and at least two whose tier is decided from another difficulty's records.

INHERITANCE AND OVERRIDES. Six overrides are declared, clause by clause, and they are the whole of what
this task's policies do differently from base.
On auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund, against auto_evt_gap_refund:
 - the flat full-refund window -> the method the extended rule states for the whole domain;
 - "The refund is paid to a PCB checking account of the borrower or by official check; it is never applied
   to the loan balance." -> the sentence entering it against the loan;
 - "After that window the refund is gap_premium times the number of whole months remaining to the scheduled
   maturity_date divided by term_months, rounded half-up to the cent, minus gap_cancellation_fee, and no
   refund is made when that is zero or less." -> "The unearned part is the refundable share of the charge
   financed at funding, multiplied by the months remaining and divided by the term the loan was written
   for, and the cancellation fee is deducted from it once it is settled." This is the sentence that retires
   the base reading of 795.00 x 28 / 60 - 50.00 = 321.00 and leaves 390.00 as the only refund the charter
   states on this world.
On auto_ext_payoff_settlement, which now also carries auto_evt_gap_refund in its base_policy_refs because
the principal its figure rests on is what that policy's write moves:
 - auto_evt_payoff_and_lien's "The payoff amount on a date is principal_balance plus
   auto_msr_accrued_interest through that date plus fees_due." -> the settlement sentence of this policy,
   which retires the base reading of 20419.63 and leaves 20308.37;
 - auto_evt_payoff_and_lien's "A loan that is paid off with GAP coverage in force earns a GAP refund under
   auto_evt_gap_refund." -> this policy's own prerequisite sentence;
 - auto_evt_gap_refund's "Paying the loan off early with GAP in force is treated as a cancellation on the
   payoff date." -> the same prerequisite sentence.
The last two are what settle the order. Base put the refund after the payoff in two places; both sentences
are now named and retired, so the only ordering rule in force is "The amount required to settle the loan in
full is fixed only after the refund owed on the waiver coverage financed with the loan stands entered on
its records", and the reverse order is excluded by the charter rather than by gold.
Everything else stands: the one-refund limit, the allocation order, the satisfaction rule, the state grace
days behind the two charges, the day count basis, the APR floor, the published cancellation fee (still what
the fall-through tier selects), the lien-release deadline, and auto_evt_gap_refund's consent sentence,
which is now followed rather than overridden - see the owner card below.

STEP 5. VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The builder replays the gold writes with the real tools onto the
seeded DB and evaluates each policy on the world as it stands just before its own write:
  refund 390.0  (months_remaining 31, share 95, unearned 415.3875, fee 25.0, checking months 63,
                 installments in twelve months 9, months on book 31)
  settlement 20308.37  (span 63, transit 1, days 64, rate 5.99, interest 211.0,
                        principal after the refund 20053.37, charges 44.0)
  factor sensitivity: refund 353.0 / 369.0 / 365.0 / 365.0 / 390.39; settlement 20410.37 / 20316.37 /
                      20314.37 / 20307.99; whole baselines 295.82 and 20429.92
  prerequisite sensitivity: skipping the refund gives a settlement of 20702.37
These are the figures written into computations.expected, factor_sensitivity and baseline_result.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking the extended yaml, the compute, the expected
values and this dossier: the caller wants the loan settled today; the settlement rule waits on the
refund owed on the coverage financed with the loan standing entered; the loan shows that coverage in
force and the ledger shows no refund entry; so the refund comes first. The refund rule gives 795.00 at
the 95 percent share his nine installments earn, over 33 months of a 60-month term once the quarter
convention his checking account's age selects is applied, less the 25.00 fee his card standing earns,
rounded half-up to the whole dollar: 390.00. The settlement rule then gives 20053.37 of principal, 64
days of interest at 5.99 percent rounded to 211.00, and the 44.00 of charges standing: 20308.37, split 44.00 / 211.00 / 20053.37, moved across by the
borrower from his other bank and posted to the loan by the agent. That is gold, reached
without the hidden assets.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Both writes are synchronous under one frozen_time: the borrower's own
instruction to close the coverage out, given on the line when the agent hands it to him, and the agent's
posting of the settlement against the money he moves across during the call. Nothing waits
on clearing, on a quote being posted out, on a title office or on any future date; the lien moving to
awaiting release is the loan record's own state, not an external event asserted as done. Every question
a real agent must ask has an answer in the persona — identity, which loan, whether he wants the figure
for today or a later date, how he will send the money, and an explicit "I have no idea" for anything he
could not know — and the cancellation instruction is
handed to him to give himself, its receipt entering the shared transcript.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Settling first and closing out the coverage afterwards
(the settlement rule waits on the refund entry, and the figure differs by 394.00). Refunding the whole
795.00 because the cancellation is treated as inside the full-refund window (the window ran out on
2024-04-09, sixty days after funding). Working the months remaining from today rather than from the
installment then due (the middle tier applies because the checking balance is under its tier's waiver
balance while three deposits posted). Taking 31 months instead of 33 (the account's age selects the
quarter convention). Deducting the published 50.00 fee (the card standing selects 25.00). Running the
interest clock from the last payment credited (94 days) instead of from the installment then due (63).
Forgetting the 44.00 of charges standing, which the allocation clears first out of the settlement.


ROUND 2 — REWORK AGAINST THE POLICY-TASK AUDIT (revision 1 of
env/regional_retail_bank/audits/policy_task/auto_loan_payment_servicing/). Item by item, for this task:
- F-C1 (RED, the charter stated the payoff/GAP order in both directions): closed. Both base sentences that
  put the refund after the payoff are now named in auto_ext_payoff_settlement.overwrite and replaced by this
  policy's prerequisite sentence. Only one order remains in force.
- F-C2 (RED, undeclared override of the base GAP pro-rata formula): closed by the third overwrite entry on
  auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund. The base reading 321.00 is a retired clause; 390.00 stands alone.
- F-C6 (RED, undeclared override of the base payoff formula): closed by the first overwrite entry on
  auto_ext_payoff_settlement. The base reading 20419.63 is a retired clause; 20308.37 stands alone.
- F-C5 (RED, the consent/owner boundary reversed): closed by putting the owners where the frozen blueprint
  puts the acts - post_gap_refund_16f4decd is now owner=user and post_loan_payoff_a84c6454 owner=agent - and
  by having the borrower's own call record the confirmed auto_requests row of request_type gap_cancellation
  that auto_evt_gap_refund asks for. Nothing is overridden here: the base sentence is now satisfiable and
  satisfied. The persona was rewritten to match: he gives the cancellation instruction himself when it is
  handed to him, and leaves the posting of the settlement to the representative while he moves the money.
- F-C12 (the author's own note confirming F-C6 was a known deviation): closed with F-C6. The BASE-INVARIANT
  CARD sentence it quotes now names the declared override rather than describing an undeclared refinement.
- T1-F2 (RED, two scored values and the write order not uniquely entailed): closed as the consequence of
  F-C1, F-C2 and F-C6. No seed, formula or gold value changed: refund_amount is still 390.00 and
  settlement_amount still 20308.37.
- T1-F3 (observation, order_uniqueness arguing from gold): acted on. prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness
  now argues from the retired base clauses and the one surviving ordering sentence, and cites the figures
  only to show what the excluded order would have produced.
- T1-F4 (observation, tier_taken stating an "exactly one" tier as an "or"): already correct in this task's
  artifacts, and now generated straight from the ladder in both tasks so it cannot drift.
- F-C13 (observation, the seeded late charges of 22.00 not following the base late-charge formula): not a
  defect once the charter is read as a whole. auto_evt_late_charge's amount sentence is superseded, charter
  wide, by auto_ext_fee_overcharge_correction's declared override, and under that method the charge this
  charter fixes for this loan is 694.07 x 4.00 percent = 27.76, ceilinged at correction_ceiling_mid 22.00
  for a loan carrying two late charges in twenty-four months, rounded half-up to the whole dollar at 31
  months on book: 22.00, exactly what the two seeded rows carry. The seeded history is one the charter's own
  fee rule does produce. Left unchanged.
- T1-F1 (observation, no near-miss in this task flips a tier): not acted on; it would need a reseed of a
  world every other section of the audit found sound.
user_scenario:
Dorian Whitesell is fifty-seven, a facilities supervisor for the county schools in Greensboro who took early retirement money out of a pension pot this month and has decided to be rid of one debt before the year turns. He is courteous and unhurried, but he knows exactly what he came for and says it in his first breath: "I want to pay this car loan off in full today. I've got the money sitting here and I'd rather not owe on that truck any more." He means the Honda he financed with the bank, and he wants it done on this call, not quoted for some later date; he says so if he is asked whether he wants a figure for today or for a future date. He will send the money from an account he keeps at another bank, and he says so when he is asked how he wants to pay, and he is content for the representative to take that money and post it to the loan for him. He is happy for the representative to make whatever entries the bank's rules require on the loan first, and he says he will give any instruction that has to come from him personally while he is on the line.

He offers no figures of his own. Asked to identify himself he gives his mobile number, 3365550588, and then, as the representative asks for more, his date of birth, 1968-11-30, the last four digits of his Social Security number, 1562, and the ZIP code on his statements, 27405. He knows he has fallen behind — "I've been slow the last couple of months, I won't pretend otherwise" — but he does not know how far behind, what has been added to the loan, or what interest has built up, and he says so plainly: "Whatever the payoff is, tell me the number and I'll send it." If he is asked for anything he could not be expected to know, such as what is still owing on the principal or how much interest has accrued since his last payment, he says he has no idea and waits for the representative to work it out.

His answers come only after the representative has said something. If the representative explains that the protection product financed with the loan has to be closed out first and the money owed back on it entered against the loan, he says, "That's fine by me, I've no use for it once the loan's gone — put it wherever it belongs." When the representative tells him that cancelling it is his own instruction to give and hands it to him, he gives it himself for the figure he is told and reads the confirmation back. When the representative then tells him what it takes to settle the loan, he answers, "Right, send it through and I'll have the money moved across today," and leaves the posting to the representative. If the representative gives him a number that sounds nothing like what he has been carrying, he says it seems off against his last statement and asks for it to be checked against the record, but he never offers a figure of his own, because he does not have one. He does not ask for a payoff letter, a receipt in the post or anything to be mailed to him.

Once the representative tells him the loan is settled and closed, he is plainly relieved and ends the call: "Well, that's a weight off. Thank you for sorting it." He raises nothing further, and if the representative never mentions the protection product he does not mention it either.

request_alignment.claim: The borrower asks for his auto loan to be settled in full today and means it to be done on this call, not quoted for a later date.
evidence: user_scenario:I want to pay this car loan off in full today.

request_alignment.claim: He authorises the representative to make whatever entries the bank's rules require on the loan first, and will make his own part himself.
evidence: user_scenario:He is happy for the representative to make whatever entries the bank's rules require on the loan first

gold_actions.business_effect: The borrower's own cancellation instruction is recorded as confirmed, the waiver coverage financed with the loan is closed out with today as its cancellation date, a refund entry of 390.00 is posted on the loan's activity, and the loan's unpaid principal falls from 20443.37 to 20053.37.

request_binding.action_semantics: The loan carries waiver coverage financed at funding that is still in force with no refund entry against it, and the unearned part of that charge is owed back whether or not the borrower raises it; the only action that state selects is closing the coverage out and entering the refund. The charter makes that cancellation the borrower's own instruction, so the agent hands the write to him. It is not a payment and it is not a fee correction.

discriminator.business_meaning: the waiver coverage financed with the loan still shown in force with no refund entered against it

stage_provenance.fact: The coverage is in force at the moment of the call, and the borrower's confirmed instruction, the closing out and the refund entry are all completed on the spot by this write.

base_preconditions.condition: Each loan receives at most one GAP refund.

gold_actions.business_effect: A settlement of 20308.37 posts to the loan, clearing 44.00 of charges, 211.00 of interest and 20053.37 of principal; the loan closes as paid off with today as its closing date and the lien moves to awaiting release.

request_binding.action_semantics: The caller asks for the whole loan to be settled today, which selects the payoff write rather than a scheduled installment payment, a quote for a future date or any change of terms. Posting a payoff is a service action, so the agent makes the write against the money the borrower moves across.

evidence: user_scenario:I want to pay this car loan off in full today.

discriminator.business_meaning: pay this car loan off in full today
evidence: user_scenario:I want to pay this car loan off in full today.

stage_provenance.fact: The refund owed on the coverage financed with the loan stands entered against it, which is what the settlement figure is worked out on.

base_preconditions.condition: Payments post only to a loan whose status is active or delinquent.

This policy fixes the shape of the payoff figure, the life of a payoff quote and the deadline for sending the lien release; its only eligibility gate governs the release itself, so on the settlement payment it applies as scope alone.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the caller's customer profile from the mobile number he states and read the credential fields the verification write is measured against.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the profile there is no customer reference number to verify against and no borrower to attach the loan lookup to.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record an in-session identity verification from the three details the caller states.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No balance may be discussed and no servicing write made until the caller is verified against the profile.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the borrower's auto loan: its product, status, unpaid principal and fees, rate, term, monthly installment, next due date, maturity date, last payment date, days past due, funding date and whether the waiver coverage financed with it is still in force.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The refund rests on the charge financed at funding, the term, the maturity and the installment then due; the settlement rests on the unpaid principal, the charges standing, the recorded rate and the funding date.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the loan ledger: the funding disbursement, every scheduled installment credited with its split, and the two late charges standing unpaid.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The count of scheduled installments credited in the last twelve months decides the refundable share and the settlement rate, and the entries fix the date the most recent entry posted, which one anchor of the settlement clock uses.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the borrower's checking account: its tier, status, posted balance and the date it was opened.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The months-remaining tier and the settlement clock anchor rest on the balance against the waiver balance its tier publishes, and the unearned-share convention on the account's age.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the checking ledger: the recurring payroll deposits of the last three months and the debits against them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The count of recurring deposits is the second limb of the months-remaining tier and of the settlement clock anchor tier.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the borrower's credit card account: its status, limit, balance owed and unredeemed reward points.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The cancellation fee tier and the transit allowance tier rest on the card's unredeemed reward points.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the card ledger: the purchases posted over the last twelve months and the payment made against the card.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The count of card purchases in the last three months decides the cancellation fee and the transit allowance, and the twelve-month purchase total decides the settlement rate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the borrower's own instruction to close out the waiver coverage so it can be handed to him.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Cancelling the coverage financed with his loan is the borrower's own instruction; the agent unlocks it and hands it over at this problem's place in the order.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The borrower gives his confirmed instruction to close out the waiver coverage financed with the loan, and the refund owed on it is entered against the loan, so the unpaid principal falls by it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund is the only policy that computes refund_amount, and the settlement figure cannot be fixed until that refund stands on the loan's records.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.auto_loan_id: Value 4f786106-e2c0-4d56-80c3-a442fa3fcd12. Basis: the auto loan lookup at action 2 returns exactly one loan for this borrower, and the tool's schema says of this argument 'the reference number of your auto loan whose waiver coverage is being closed out; the servicing agent reads it from the loan record and hands it over with this tool'. Uniqueness: the borrower holds one auto loan, and it is the one carrying the coverage.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value fa341524-a7a6-47a0-a176-2eb09ddd7bf5. Basis: the customer lookup at action 0 returns one profile for the mobile number the caller states, and the tool's schema says of this argument 'the reference number identifying you as the borrower on that loan; the servicing agent reads it from your customer profile and hands it over'. Uniqueness: one profile matches, and the loan row's own borrower reference equals it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_amount: Value 390.0. auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund computes it on the opening world. Refundable share: 9 scheduled installments were credited to the loan in the last twelve months, at least the mid count of 8 and fewer than the deep count of 12, so the share is 95 percent of the 795.00 charge financed at funding, 755.25. Months remaining: the checking balance of 3167.25 is under the 10000.00 fee-waiver daily balance Premier Checking publishes, so the first limb fails, while three recurring payroll deposits posted in the last three months carry the second, so exactly one of the two holds and the months remaining run from the installment then due, 2026-07-15, to the maturity of 2029-02-15, which is 31. Unearned share: the checking account opened 2021-05-20 is 63 whole months old, at least the mid seasoning of 48 and under the long seasoning of 120, so the months remaining are taken up to the whole quarter above, 33, and 755.25 times 33 over the 60-month term is 415.3875. Cancellation fee: the card carries 9800 unredeemed points and 7 purchases in the last three months, both over the mid thresholds and under the deep, so the fee is 25.00, leaving 390.3875. Rounding: the loan funded 2024-02-09 is 31 whole months old, at least the mid seasoning of 24 and under the long seasoning of 36, so the refund is rounded half-up to the whole dollar, 390.0.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the servicing write that posts the borrower's settlement to the loan and closes it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the problem the caller actually raised; it changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Post the borrower's settlement of the whole loan, clearing the charges standing, the interest owed and the unpaid principal, so the loan closes and the lien moves to awaiting release.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: auto_ext_payoff_settlement is the only policy that computes settlement_amount; it is the root problem of this task and the terminal state the caller is waiting for.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.auto_loan_id: Value 4f786106-e2c0-4d56-80c3-a442fa3fcd12. Basis: the tool's schema says of this argument 'the reference number of the auto loan being settled; read it from the loan record returned by the auto loan lookup before the call'. Uniqueness: the borrower holds exactly one auto loan.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Value fa341524-a7a6-47a0-a176-2eb09ddd7bf5. Basis: the tool's schema says 'the reference number identifying the borrower on that loan; read it from the customer profile lookup before the call'. Uniqueness: the single customer profile returned at action 0.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount: Value 20308.37. auto_ext_payoff_settlement computes it on the world after the refund has been entered. Unpaid principal: 20443.37 less the 390.00 refund entered against the loan, 20053.37. Clock anchor: the checking balance is under its tier's waiver balance while three recurring deposits posted in the last three months, so exactly one limb holds and the clock runs from the installment then due, 2026-07-15, to today, 63 days. Transit allowance: 9800 reward points and 7 card purchases in three months put it on its middle rung, 1 day, so the clock runs 64 days. Settlement rate: card purchases of 6950.00 over twelve months are at least the mid threshold of 3000.00 and under the deep threshold of 12000.00 and 9 installments were credited in twelve months, so the rate is the recorded 6.24 less the published automatic-payment reduction of 0.25, 5.99. Interest: 20053.37 at 5.99 percent divided by 365 and multiplied by 64 is 210.62, and the loan being 31 whole months old that is rounded half-up to the whole dollar, 211.00. With the 44.00 of charges standing, the settlement is 20053.37 + 211.00 + 44.00 = 20308.37.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fees_portion: Value 44.0. Basis: the charter's allocation sentence, inherited by this policy, states that each payment is applied 'first to fees_due, then to interest accrued through the credit date, then to principal', and the loan carries two late charges of 22.00 standing unpaid. Uniqueness: the standing figure is one ledger quantity and the settlement is larger than it, so the whole 44.00 is cleared.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.interest_portion: Value 211.0. Basis: the same allocation sentence puts the interest accrued through the credit date next, and this policy fixes that interest at 211.00 as drawn out above. Uniqueness: the interest for the credit date is the single figure this policy's interest rule produces.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.principal_portion: Value 20053.37. Basis: the allocation sentence ends with principal, so 20308.37 less 44.0 and 211.0, which is exactly the unpaid principal the records then show and takes it to zero. Uniqueness: the remainder of a fixed total after two fixed parts admits one value.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_channel: Value external_ach. Basis: the caller says 'He will send the money from an account he keeps at another bank', and the tool's schema says to 'Pass external_ach where the money is drawn from an account the borrower holds at another bank'. Uniqueness: none is excluded because this is a payment; autopay_pcb is excluded because the loan carries no standing draft and he is settling in one go; pcb_transfer is excluded because the money does not come from a Piedmont Crescent account; mail_check is excluded because no paper check is posted; branch is excluded because he is on the telephone; debit_card_phone is excluded because he offers no card, he is moving funds from the other bank.

edges.condition: The loan's records carry a refund entry for the waiver coverage financed with it, and that coverage is no longer shown as in force.
edges.policy_source: The amount required to settle the loan in full is fixed only after the refund owed on the waiver coverage financed with the loan stands entered on its records.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At the frozen date the loan still shows the waiver coverage financed at funding in force, with no cancellation date and no refund entry anywhere on its ledger, so nothing has been entered against the principal.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The refund write closes the coverage out, dates the cancellation today and posts a refund entry of 390.00 on the loan, so the unpaid principal the settlement is worked out on becomes 20053.37 and the settlement figure 20308.37 instead of 20702.37.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain of two problems with a single edge, so there is only one topological order: the refund is entered and then the settlement is posted. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder. The reverse order is not merely different, it is outside the charter as it stands. Base put the refund after the payoff in two sentences - auto_evt_payoff_and_lien's 'A loan that is paid off with GAP coverage in force earns a GAP refund under auto_evt_gap_refund.' and auto_evt_gap_refund's 'Paying the loan off early with GAP in force is treated as a cancellation on the payoff date.' - and auto_ext_payoff_settlement.overwrite now names both and replaces each with its own sentence 'The amount required to settle the loan in full is fixed only after the refund owed on the waiver coverage financed with the loan stands entered on its records.' Both are therefore retired, and that sentence is the only ordering rule left in force. Had the settlement been posted first it would have been worked out on the seeded principal of 20443.37 and come to 20702.37, and the refund would afterwards have fallen on a loan already at zero principal and closed - which is what the retired clauses would have produced and what the surviving one forbids.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the refund leaves the unpaid principal at 20443.37, so the settlement figure becomes 20702.37 instead of 20308.37, the principal portion of the payment 20443.37 instead of 20053.37, and the loan's ledger carries no refund entry at all.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario names no prerequisite problem and nothing the refund resolves. The caller asks only to settle the loan; he never mentions the waiver coverage, a refund, a cancellation or anything owed back, and he asks no leading question about whether something must be dealt with first. His only line on the subject is the reaction written for after the representative has explained it, and the closing note says explicitly that if the representative never mentions the protection product he does not mention it either.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither tool validates a prerequisite. post_loan_payoff_a84c6454 writes the settlement entry and closes the loan with the arguments exactly as passed; it makes no test of gap_coverage, of whether a refund entry stands on the loan, or of the principal it is given, and it returns its ordinary receipt whatever the state of the coverage. post_gap_refund_16f4decd likewise records the confirmed cancellation request, books its entry and reduces the principal with no test of its own. The consequence of settling before the refund is entered shows up only in the terminal hash.

factor_trace: remaining_months_measure (method): the checking balance of 3167.25 is under the 10000.00 fee-waiver daily balance Premier Checking publishes, so the first limb fails, while the payroll deposits of 3184.90 posted 2026-07-01, 2026-08-03 and 2026-09-01 carry the second, so exactly one of the two holds and the months remaining run from the installment then due, 2026-07-15, to the maturity of 2029-02-15, 31 whole months; the baseline takes the 60-month term less the 31 whole months since funding, 29, and would give 353.00.

refundable_share_step (parameter): 9 scheduled installments were credited to the loan in the last twelve months, from 2025-10-14 to 2026-06-14, at least the mid count of 8 and fewer than the deep count of 12, so the refundable share is 95 percent; the baseline share of 90 percent would give 369.00.

unearned_share_convention (method): the checking account opened 2021-05-20 is 63 whole months old, at least the mid seasoning of 48 and under the long seasoning of 120, so the months remaining are taken up to the whole quarter above, 33, and the unearned part is 755.25 times 33 over 60, 415.3875; the baseline measures it on the whole months remaining, 31, and would give 365.00.

cancellation_fee_step (parameter): the card carries 9800 unredeemed reward points and 7 purchases posted in the last three months, both over the mid thresholds of 5000 and 3 and under the deep thresholds of 25000 and 12, so the fee is 25.00; the baseline fee is the 50.00 the product publishes and would give 365.00.

refund_rounding (method): the loan funded 2024-02-09 is 31 whole months old, at least the mid seasoning of 24 and under the long seasoning of 36, so 390.3875 is rounded half-up to the whole dollar, 390.00; the baseline rounds half-up to the cent and would give 390.39.

bindings belonging to no factor: premium_financed and loan_term read the charge financed at funding and the term; refundable_premium, refund_before_rounding and result are arithmetic, result holding the refund at nothing where the figure comes out at nothing or less.
